question: What will our 2026 accident-year loss ratio be?
final_text:
I can't give a 2026 accident-year loss ratio from this data. The 2026 accident year hasn't started, and the tools only report actual experience. Any figure would be a forecast that needs assumptions about 2026 pricing, mix, claims inflation, and reserving, none of which are in the data.

For context, the accident-year ultimate loss ratio (reported loss + IBNR, over earned premium, as at 31 Dec 2025) has been:

| Accident year | Loss ratio (ultimate) | Earned premium (GBP) |
|---|---|---|
| 2021 | 0.603 | 14,999,153 |
| 2022 | 0.823 | 18,519,655 |
| 2023 | 0.921 | 21,311,739 |
| 2024 | 0.819 | 23,748,558 |
| 2025 | 0.782 | 27,877,321 |

The 2023–2025 results average roughly 0.84, and the most recent year is 0.78. The 2025 figure still depends on IBNR estimates, so it may move as the year develops. These are historical reference points, not a forecast.

ANSWER: UNANSWERABLE
